comments.text: Line 0: REM, five DEL characters and a shifted L, the guard five of the game's six BASIC programs start with (all but B; BEGIN's is line 1): LIST rubs out "0 REM" and stops with ?SYNTAX ERROR at the shifted L.

Line 1 turns off CIA 1's interrupts (56333) and RESTORE (the NMI vector to $FEC1, an RTI), lowers BASIC's top to $1300, below the engine's tables at $1400, and clears the variables. Line 2 is the program: the constants (19000), the flight's variables (900), the flight (15000), then the disk turned for the debriefing (1000).
Line 7 writes ZV as a word, low byte first, to the engine's variable V: zero-page address V in the copy at $3F00 (SV). Line 8 reads one back into ZV; nothing calls it.
Lines 10 and 11 copy L pages from page F to page T with the helper at $8014 (M6). Nothing calls them, and line 2's F, $8100, is not a page number.

Line 900 clears $3F00-$3FFF, the engine's zero page, with the helper at $8029 (SB). Line 905 names the SID, the stores at $53D8 (OD) and the units at $5100 (EN); line 920 copies the six stores counts from the front end's record at $0350 into $53D8-$53DD. Lines 930-936 copy words of that record ($033C on) into the engine's variables named by the DATA, through line 990: line 931 puts words 1-9 at $7C (night), $7F (3 less the enemy's quality), the words $70 and $72 (the two tanks' fuel), $4B (the flying realism times 2 plus the landings'), $4C (the style plus 1, or 0 in training), $39 (the heat) and $4F and $50 (the wind).
Lines 940 and 941: the waypoint, engine words $76 and $78, is put on the first unit of the primary target ($53E1 gives its number): the high bytes of that unit's x and y times 256.

Lines 950-955 colour the cockpit window: DATA sets 0 to the theatre's number ($035E), or all six at night ($033E), each passed to the helper at $8099, so the last one read stays. A set is the window's colour-RAM colour, its two screen colours, and its background, which also goes to zpa_C4 and to four of the picture's colour cells below the window's corners.
A false label in line 955's DATA: the BIT at $7981 hides an LDA #$0A and names this address by chance.

Line 989 ends line 900's subroutine. Lines 990-993 copy one word of the front end's record ($033C + 2I) to the engine's variable read from DATA; a number of 256 or more is a word at that number less 256, written by line 7, else one byte.

Lines 1000-1062, after the flight: the drive is asked to initialise ("i0:") until it finds side 2 again, asking for it back side up and waiting for fire; then LOAD "b",8,1 is printed with a RETURN in the keyboard buffer and NEW, so BASIC loads the debriefing.

Lines 15000-15003 start the flight: border black, screen off, the mission bits at $7043 from the front end's $03B4, the SID's voice 2 sustain set; the cockpit picture's colours copied from $4000 to colour RAM, the second window bitmap from $6000 to $4000. Then the STOP vector goes back to the KERNAL's $F6ED and LOAD "awh" runs: AWH's few bytes overwrite the stack, so the LOAD returns into the engine at $3100.

Line 16000 runs when the engine returns: colour RAM copied back to $4000 (SYS MVB, read as MV, since BASIC keeps two letters of a name). Line 16001 turns the border and background white and the SID's volume off.

Lines 19000-19004, the constants: FNLB gives a word's low byte; SB, MV, BM, KE, S6 and M6 are the helpers in $8000-$80E2; A0-A6 their parameter bytes $A5-$AB; KP and KK 256 and 65536; SV the engine's zero page at $3F00.
The program's end, then 161 bytes the file still holds: tokenised lines of the side 2 loader (POKE A0... SYS KE, its SETNAM and LOAD calls). BASIC's variables start after them, at $0E75.

Shape: the Mi-24 Hind, the enemy helicopter, ten points and six faces; colour byte $81. Used as the Hind's object at $1E9F.

The flight's start and end. The load of AWH, the last file G2 loads, ends in an RTS to here: $30FF was on the stack above BASIC's own return into LOAD ($E177). Starts the engine ($8115), runs the main loop until the flight ends, leaves a map or picture view if one is up ($8112), stops the engine ($8118) and blanks the screen. The two PLAs drop BASIC's return into LOAD, so the RTS goes back to BASIC's statement loop and G2 runs on from the statement after its LOAD, with its variables kept.

The top of the main loop, once a pass. A damaged engine (damage bits 2 and 3) cannot run: its bit in zpa_44 is cleared. With both fuel tanks empty both engines stop, their sounds end, and a helicopter sitting on the ground with no landing recorded counts as landed (zpa_86 = 2).

The first pass only (zpa_4E still 0): the jammers off, the two engine gauges ($8141, $8143) set to $80 so they drop to nothing at once, the lamps set for the starting state, the stores counted (count_load), the cannon selected and its lamp lit, and sprite 2's pointer in the panel ($EFFA) set to $C0.

Every pass: the pass counter zpa_6A-zpa_6B, the flight's clock, goes up; zpa_51 counts down. The helicopter's position (zpa_5E-zpa_61) and height (zpa_62-zpa_63) are copied to $812D-$8132 and $814E-$8153 for the 3D view and the map, the eye 24 units above the helicopter; the view's heading (minus the helicopter's heading zpa_34 and the look direction zpa_37), its pitch and its roll go to $8133-$8135.

The chaff and flare timers (zpa_46, zpa_47) count down, their lamps ($19, $1B) lit while they run. Then the 3D view is drawn (s_8106). The sight, sprite 0, is shown ($815C = $55) only when looking ahead. If the view drawing found the eye inside a hill (zpa_05), the flight ends as a crash: zpa_82 = 1.

Moves the missiles and shells (s_819C) and draws the radar scope (s_81AF). A hit on the helicopter ($81B3) is damage (hit_helicopter, effect 5); a missile caught by chaff or flares ($81B2) makes sound 7; a unit hit by the player's missile ($81B4) is destroyed (destroy_unit).

The seven bar gauges' values, which s_811B draws: the fore and aft fuel ($813D, $813E), each engine's torque from the collective while it runs ($813F, $8140), the rotor speed ($8142); $8141 and $8143 are each engine's bar, full while it runs. Then the heading ($8144); the pitch, clamped to -$14 to $13 ($813A), and the roll, negated ($813B). With the forward avionics hit (damage bit 4) all seven bars show $80: nothing.

Draws the attitude indicator (s_811E); then the airspeed needle's angle ($8137, three quarters of the speed zpa_6C), the height times 1.25 ($8145-$8146) and the vertical speed as a needle angle ($8139, from the sine table at $C600) for the dials, which s_811B draws. Then the buffers are swapped (s_810F) and one key is taken from the keyboard buffer (get_key).

The keys. $FF, RESTORE with RUN/STOP, aborts the flight (zpa_82 = $80). ← on the big map toggles fast motion (zpa_85) and shows it in the border, light red when on. SPACE steps the CRT display on (s_810C). Z shows the big map (s_8112 with 1); C= ($7E) and left SHIFT ($7D) show the stores and damage pictures (s_8112 with 2 and 3), which are loaded from disk.

RUN/STOP ($7F) pauses: the sound off until a key is pressed; RESTORE with RUN/STOP still aborts. Right SHIFT ($7C) asks for the next target (zpa_FA = 1). HOME looks ahead, £ and DEL look to the two sides (zpa_37 = 0, $E0 and $20). F1, F3, F5 and F7 move the collective (zpa_3A) by +4, +1, -1 and -4, kept between 0 and 42.

Keys 1 and 2 start and stop engines 1 and 2 (bits 0 and 1 of zpa_44), only while there is fuel and the engine is not damaged (damage bits 2 and 3), with the starter's sound; the engine's bar ($8141, $8143) is filled or emptied. Key 3 engages and frees the rotor's clutch (bit 2); freeing it drops the collective to 0, and the clutch lamp ($0E) shows which.

RETURN stops the turn (zpa_40 = 0). Keys 4, 5, 6 and 7 choose the Sidewinders, the FFARs, the Hellfires and the cannon (zpa_43 = 1, 2, 3, 0), lighting the weapon's lamp ($16, $17, $18, $1A) after weapon_lamps_off has put the others out.

Key 9 fires chaff, when the chaff launcher works (damage bit 13): one from the store at $53DD, and the chaff timer zpa_46 set to 36. The - key fires a flare the same way, when the flare launcher works (bit 7): the store at $53DC and the timer zpa_47.

Key 0 turns the radar jammer on and off (bit 4 of zpa_44, $81AA) and + the infrared jammer (bit 3, $81AB), each lighting its lamp ($12, $13); neither works with the aft avionics hit (damage bit 5). The cursor keys turn: CRSR right/left adds 1 to the turn rate zpa_40 and CRSR down/up takes 1 off.

The turn rate is kept between -4 and 4, and stopped when the speed zpa_7B is 15 or more either way: the helicopter turns on the spot only when slow. RESTORE with 4, 5 or 6 ($B4-$B6) jettisons all the Sidewinders, FFARs or Hellfires, with sound 2, and the load is counted again.
The missiles' weight, zpa_3C: twice the Sidewinders, FFARs and Hellfires together, plus the Hellfires again; then the stores numbers are redrawn (draw_stores).

The joystick, read (joystick) into zpa_84 (left -1, right +1) and zpa_7A (up -1, down +1). On the big map (zpa_18 = 1) it moves the waypoint, zpa_76-zpa_79, and its cross (sprite 0), for as long as it is held, and the flying goes on without it.

In the cockpit: the bearing from the helicopter to the waypoint (bearing on the two differences) goes to $813C and is printed (s_812A); against the heading it places sprite 3, the waypoint's mark on the heading strip ($8178). The direction of travel zpa_3E against the heading places sprite 2, the slip mark ($8177).

The stick's roll: zpa_84 times 4 is added to the roll zpa_36, kept within ±20; a main rotor hit (damage bit 0) adds a random shake. Pushing the stick changes the pitch zpa_35; hovering low over the ground (height below zpa_6C, climbing) adds a random pitch kick.

The lift, zpa_38: the collective, at most the rotor speed / 4 + 4. With realistic flight (bit 1 of zpa_4B) it gains up to 9 from the speed and loses the missiles' weight / 8, the heat (zpa_39) and the fuel's weight; with the rotor's clutch free it loses the vertical speed / 4. Kept between 0 and 45.

Turning. On the ground nothing turns. With the nose about level (pitch 0 to -3) the turn rate turns the helicopter on the spot, and a roll makes it slide sideways; otherwise the roll banks it round and the heading follows the direction of travel. A hit on either rotor (damage bits 0 and 1) adds a random yaw.

The lift is split by the pitch and the roll (s_8109, the sine product) into an upward part, zpa_3B, less the height's high byte, and a push, zpa_80-zpa_81: forward from the pitch, or sideways from the roll when the pitch is 0.

The vertical speed zpa_3F moves a quarter of the way towards zpa_3B, the lift's upward part, less 104, with a ground cushion of (64 less the height) / 4 below height 26 when slow (realistic flight only). The height zpa_62-zpa_63 then changes by a quarter of the vertical speed (after adding 1 and bit 0 of zpa_6A), never below 0.

Touchdown, the pass the height reaches 0. A hard one (the speed and the sink rate together $60 or more) is a crash, zpa_82 = 1, with sound 7 and the screen shaken, when landings are realistic (bit 0 of zpa_4B) or both engines are damaged. Otherwise the landing's grade, zpa_86: 2 plus that sum over 32, one more when rolled 10 or more, unless it is 4. On the ground the speeds, the pitch and the roll are zeroed.

The speed zpa_6C-zpa_6D moves a sixteenth of the way towards the push (less a part of the vertical speed by the pitch), and zpa_7B is a quarter of it. The helicopter moves by it along the direction of travel zpa_3E, in x then in y, each kept on the map by keep_on_map.
Keeps a coordinate's high byte between $18 and $D8: x indexes the coordinate's two bytes in zero page.
The wind: every second pass while airborne, zpa_4F and zpa_50, from the mission block, are added to the position.

The rotor. The engines running give a target speed for it, zpa_42, from the table at $E400 (none, one, the other or both) less twice the collective, at most 156. With the clutch in, the rotor speed zpa_41 moves an eighth of the way towards it; with it free the rotor slows by a quarter of the collective, a little more on the ground, the forward speed keeping it turning, and stops at 0.
The rotor sound: SID voice 2's frequency is the rotor speed, its pulse width from the height. Voice 3, the engines' whine, follows the speed while an engine runs, and is silent otherwise.
A cannon hit decided last pass (zpa_4A): a positive one destroys its unit (destroy_unit); a negative one, every second pass, makes sound 7 and the gun's flash, and becomes positive.
With the CRT on the map or a message (zpa_FF not 0): the fire button with a target picked (zpa_FA = 2) moves the CRT on (s_810C), with sound 8, and nothing is fired. Then on to the units.

Aiming, with the CRT on the target view: how far the target's box, sprite 1, is from the middle of the window ($8155, $815D) is the aim error zpa_64-zpa_65; looking to the side it is $7F. The locked target's unit (s_81C4) is zpa_3D, $7F for none. Its record is read (unit_read) and, the first time, marked identified (bit 4 of its type byte) and the map redrawn.

The distance to the target, zpa_7D-zpa_7E, is the difference in x plus the difference in y. With the aim error, scaled for the weapon, it gives a class 0 to 3; the target box's colour, $8165, comes from the table at $53A4 by that class, one step lighter at night.

The fire button (zpa_CA). Firing lets the units see the helicopter from further for a while: zpa_51 = 50 passes, 114 at night. The cannon ($3D7E on) uses a round from $53D8, recoils the nose, and hits when a random fraction of a range is beyond the target's distance; the range shrinks with a worse aim, with the style (zpa_4C) and with the gun damaged (damage bit 12). zpa_4A is then the target with bit 7 set. Ground units of type 3 can be hit only on every fourth pass.

One ground unit's turn, unit zpa_45. Its record is read (unit_read); a destroyed one (type 0) is skipped. Its type's attributes, zpa_5A, come from $53A8. The differences to the helicopter in x and y, zpa_66-zpa_69 (in quarters), and their sum zpa_6E-zpa_6F are worked out.

Whether it sees the helicopter: not beyond the height plus half the speed plus zpa_51 (twice that for a radar unit while the radar jammer is on); a unit without radar not beyond its own range ($800 for types with bit 4, half at night); a radar unit already tracking loses it while the jammer or chaff works; not behind a hill (hill_between). Friendly units ($20 in the type byte) never engage.
If it can, its alert count (bits 3-4 of zpa_57) goes up. At 1 it is put on the radar scope (s_81A2) and marked seen on the map; at 2 a radar unit lights the radar warning (zpa_48); at 3 it fires.

A gun unit (attributes 0-2) shoots within (its attributes + 1) × $800: a hit, damage effect 7 (hit_helicopter), when a random fraction of that beats the distance; a miss puts the count back. A missile unit launches one (s_819F) from where it stands at the helicopter's bearing, of its own type, when fewer than four enemy missiles fly ($81AE), with sound 8. Either way the count starts again (unit_calm).

After the last unit of this pass: the threat lamps. With the aft avionics working, lamp $0F lights for a radar missile homing on the helicopter (bit 7 of $81AE) or flashes while a radar unit tracks it (zpa_48), and lamp $10 for an infrared one (bit 6); with them hit, all five lamps $0F-$13 are out and both jammers off.

What is under the helicopter (s_81CA): over map character $26, a friendly base, with a mission done and no challenge yet ($7043 below 4), the challenge for the password starts (zpa_88 = 1). Then the challenge's own step (challenge).

The Hind, unit 5, when it is in the air (x not 0). It flies at the helicopter, or back towards its base, the unit at $53FB, while the helicopter is over a friendly base (or the hill test at the Hind's own point is set).

Its heading zpa_52 turns two steps a pass towards the bearing it wants (straight to it when going home). Seeing the helicopter, with no hill between at three points on the way, and pointing nearly at it, it fires: a hit, damage effect 7 (hit_helicopter), when a random fraction of a range set by the style (doubled by day) is beyond the distance.
It flies 50 units a pass along its heading, at 32 below the helicopter's height (at least 24), and its record is written back.

Every sixteenth pass: has the helicopter landed and stopped (landed_check)? If the flight has ended (zpa_82 not 0) the Hind is grounded, the units on the radar scope are taken off it, the missiles cleared ($81AC), and the main loop returns.

Otherwise fuel is burnt: with both engines running the collective times three from each tank, with one half that, with none nothing; a tank burns double when the other is empty, and a leak (damage bits 8 and 9) takes $60 more. Neither goes below 0.

On a random chance by the style (zpa_4C): a grounded Hind is sent up again from its base ($53FB), if that unit still stands, with the message "ENEMY HIND HELICOPTER AIRBORNE" (7); or, once in 256 passes with the Hind up and no mission done, the primary and secondary targets swap (s_7044), with message 6. With the nose optics hit (damage bit 6) the CRT changes display by itself (s_810C). Then round again.
Starts sound effect zpa_6E (s_8197 with the table at $EC00), the volume full.
A unit whose alert count is not 0 is taken off the radar scope (s_81A5); a radar unit that had reached 2 stops lighting the warning (zpa_48 down by one). The count is cleared.
Lights panel lamp zpa_33 in colour zpa_6E (s_81B5). Numbers below 14 are the damage word's bits, put in lamp numbers by the table at $53B8.
Puts the five weapon lamps $16-$1A out (colour 14).
Takes one from store x ($53D8 on: rounds, Sidewinders, FFARs, Hellfires, flares, chaff) and redraws the numbers; A is 1 if there was one, 0 if the store was empty.
Prints the six stores numbers on the panel, each at its place from the tables at $5398 and $539E.

Destroys unit zpa_6E. The Hind (5) is taken out of the air and counted in zpa_83. Any other has its bit cleared in the map's page at $E200, its type byte zeroed (the old one kept at $5200) and the map redrawn; a friendly one ($20 in its type byte) brings the message "CEASE FIRE ... FRIENDLY TROOPS HAVE BEEN HIT" (8); otherwise the missions are checked (s_7040), and a mission completed brings message 9 or 10.
The hit chances out of 16, by the attacker's attributes (zpa_5A & 7): 4, 8, always, 8, then always for 4-7.

The helicopter is hit, by effect zpa_6E. It can miss: a random 0-15 against the table at $5ADD by the attacker's attributes, then the pass counter's low two bits against zpa_4C, the style plus 1 on a mission and 0 in training: in training nothing ever hits, and on a mission a quarter, a half or three quarters of the shots that pass the first test hit, by the style. Otherwise a random bit of the damage word is set (s_8103 for 0-13); an engine hit stops its gauge; a wing halves the missiles, or empties them with the other wing gone too. Every hit shakes the screen and counts in zpa_4D, and more than 7 less zpa_4C stop both engines.
The sound, the border's flash, and the damage lamps redrawn.
Lights the 14 damage lamps from the damage word zpa_74-zpa_75: in the colour from $53C8 (yellow or light red) for a set bit, green for a clear one.
Every sixteenth pass: with both engines off, the rotor below 32, the helicopter on the ground and a landing graded (zpa_86), the flight ends with that grade, zpa_82.

Twice the differences zpa_66-zpa_69 added to the unit's position, put through the map's hill test (s_81CA): A5 and A6 are not 0 when that point is on a hill. Run three times along the line, it says whether a hill hides the helicopter.
