The horizon middle's y, high byte, patched in.
The y of the horizon's left end, low byte, patched in.
Its high byte. The left half of the horizon, from its middle 128 pixels to the left, clipped (line_clip), and the ground's edge along the window's top when the line leaves it.

The heading eighth's first entry in the order of squares ($8281), patched in. The nine squares are drawn from the farthest to the nearest: the ground's objects of each square's kind, from the lists at $1DD7 (how many), $1DF8 and $1E19 (where). Then, unless the big map is up in fast motion, the sky is filled down to them (fill_sky), the horizon drawn again in colour 0 with the line routines set to rub out ($31) and back to draw ($11), and the squares drawn again with the units on them: the units' lists at $1E3A, $1E5B and $1E7C, a bit for each unit from the square's byte at $E200 saying which still stand. Then the Hind, its shape at $1E9F, and the CRT (crt_update), and last the missiles, six objects from $1EA5, a bit each from $81AC.
Writes the opcode in A into the line routines' plotting instructions: ORA (zp),Y ($11) draws, AND (zp),Y ($31) rubs out. $86D6 does only the five that line uses.
Writes A into the five plotting instructions of the shallow and level lines, which the horizon is drawn with: ORA (zp),Y ($11) draws, AND (zp),Y ($31) rubs out.

Draws zpa_BC objects from the list at zpa_AC, six bytes each. Each is placed through the rotated corners at $1400-$1789, skipped when behind the eye or out of the window, its detail chosen by distance ($8234), its points projected (project) and its edges drawn; a hill ($FF) is filled. Each drawn object is offered as a target (target_pick).
The object's distance ahead, halved, high byte, patched in.

Its low byte, the object's centre distance plus its size ($822A, $822F), patched in. An object too far to one side or above is skipped. The distance picks the detail: nearer than $8234 says, the shape at the entry's bytes 4 and 5, else the plainer one at bytes 2 and 3; none, nothing is drawn; $FF, a hill (hill). The first object of each square starts a hill's extent ($8242-$8266). In the ground pass (zpa_0A = 0) the object's extent and distance go to the next slot of $8242-$8266, for behind_hill. Then its points are projected and its edges drawn (project); when a target is being picked it is offered (target_pick) instead. In the ground pass a line is then drawn along the window's top row between zpa_09 and zpa_08, the x range the line clipper noted, and the slot is kept when the object was drawn. The next object's entry is six bytes on.
A hill: its points projected, its outline drawn and filled; whether the eye is inside it is noted for the crash test.
Whether the object lies behind a hill drawn already, by the hills' extents in $8242-$8266; if so it is not drawn.
The x of the hill's projected first point, held to 0 to $7F, patched in.

Its y, held to 0 to $5F, patched in. The point is checked against each hill drawn so far ($8242-$8266): one that lies behind a hill, farther and inside its extent, is not drawn, and the drawing of the object is abandoned.

Projects an object's points: for each, the rotated offsets of its corners are summed into eye space ($195E on), and perspective makes screen x and y ($19DC-$1A18). Then its faces: a face is drawn when its points turn the right way round; a hill's faces facing the eye set zpa_05, the eye inside a hill.

The object's centre in eye space, patched in by draw_objects and by the target view: its sideways offset, low byte. Each of the shape's points is an entry in the rotated tables at $1400-$1789; with the centre added its offsets go to $195E-$19C7, and a point in front of the eye is projected (perspective); the first is checked against the hills (behind_hill).
The centre's sideways offset, high byte, patched in.
The centre's up-down offset, low byte, patched in.
The centre's up-down offset, high byte, patched in.
The centre's distance ahead, low byte, patched in.

The centre's distance ahead, high byte, patched in. Then the shape's faces, as many as its list says: a face with two of its three points behind the eye is hidden; for the rest, the face's angle is turned by the heading and the pitch through the sine table at $C600 and the face is turned towards the eye or away; the verdicts go to $1A7C. When none of an object's faces is turned towards the eye, the eye is inside it: zpa_05 is set, a crash.

The heading the shape is seen from, patched in: the view's ($8133) for the ground and the units, the Hind's own (zpa_04) for the Hind, the target's in the target view. Then the edges, in colour 2 in the ground pass, else in the shape's own colour; a colour with bit 7 set draws the edges first with the line routines set to rub out, then again in that colour ($8BA2). Each edge is drawn when a face beside it is turned towards the eye: a line between its two projected points, cut where it passes behind the eye (clip_near) and clipped (line_clip), or a single point (dot).
Plots a single point at its screen place, when it lies in the window.
The window's width, patched in: $7F, or $27 for the CRT's target view.
The window's height, $5F, or $2F for the target view, patched in. A point inside it is plotted (plot). The rest draws one edge between two projected points.

An RTS, made a NOP while a shape whose colour has bit 7 set is drawn: then the instructions after it run, which put the line routines back to drawing (ORA, set_plot_op), make this an RTS again and draw the edges a second time in the shape's colour ($8BAE) from the start of its list ($8BB0).
The shape's colour, patched in.
The place of its edges in the shape's list, patched in.
Divides a point's x and height by its distance (divide twice) and turns them by the roll (roll_scale), adding the window's middle: screen x in $19DC-$19F0, y in $1A04-$1A18.
The point's number, patched in, so that Y holds it again after the divide.
The point's distance, patched in for the second divide. The sideways offset divided by it, plus the up-down offset divided by it, are turned by the roll (roll_scale) to give the screen's x and y.
The point's number again, patched in.
The window's middle x, $40, patched in: the target view moves it to the CRT's.
The middle x's high byte, patched in.
The window's middle y, $30, patched in; the target view moves it.
The middle y's high byte, patched in. The point's screen x and y go to $19DC-$1A18.
Widens the extent of hill x by a point's x (A) and y (Y).
The roll's scale for roll_scale by the roll's size, six steps: the low bytes of the JMP's target.
The same, high bytes: all $8C.
Scales a value for the roll; its sign comes from zpa_A7.
Where the roll's scaling jumps, low byte, patched in from $8C76 by the roll's size: to $8C98 for none, else to one of the sequences of shifts below that multiply by 1/8, 3/16, 1/4, 3/8 or 1/2.
Where the roll's scaling jumps, high byte, from $8C7C.
Clips an edge that crosses the plane just ahead of the eye: halves the edge until its end lies in front, nine times, then projects the new end.

A BPL, made a BMI ($30) for one step when adding the two ends' distances overflowed, so that the halved sum keeps its sign. The edge's end behind the eye is moved halfway towards the other, nine times, each time to whichever half crosses: first the distance, then the sideways offsets.
The same BPL for the sideways offsets' sum. Then the up-down offsets.
The same BPL for the up-down offsets' sum.

Which end of the line the new point replaces, patched in: 0 for (zpa_19, zpa_1B), 4 for (zpa_1D, zpa_1F). A new end still behind the eye is put on the eye's plane; the point is projected (perspective) and copied there.
Copies one end of an edge, from point x, into the clipper's slots at $19C5-$19DB.

Builds the points' eye-space offsets, $1400-$1789: each point is a combination of one x value, one y value and one height, numbered for it at $1C37, $1CA8 and $1D19, and its three offsets (sideways at $1400 and $1497, up-down at $152E and $15C5, ahead at $165C and $16F3) are sums of the rotated values rotate_axes made. How many points is patched in at $8DD8; after them, unless $8E6B skips it, come the points that are a fraction of another (the lists at $1D8A on: which point, and how many halvings).
How many points to work out, less one, patched in by view_frame: 25 for the moving objects alone, or the count at $1C36 for all of them.
The carry of the sideways offset's sum, patched in, added to its high byte.
The carry of the distance's sum, patched in.
The branch's offset, patched in: 3 skips the points that are fractions of others, 6 makes them. Each of those is the point at $1D8B, shifted right as many times as $1DB1 says, keeping its sign.

One frame of the 3D view, $8106: the map's cross or the picture's own code (map_cross), the hidden bitmap's window cleared (clear_window), the squares in view found (view_squares). The coordinate values are rotated (rotate_axes) for the view's heading and pitch, and again for the Hind's heading. When the heading and pitch are those of the last frame (zpa_F3, zpa_F4) only the first 26 points are worked out again (rotate_points), the moving objects'; otherwise all of them, as many as $1C36 says, with the fractions. Then the drawing (draw_view).

Rotates the coordinate values into eye space by the heading in zpa_04 and the pitch ($8134), with the sine table at $C600: each x value ($1B88, $1BA5) gives three components, sideways ($178A), ahead ($17C4) and up ($17FE), with their high bytes after; each y value ($1BC4, $1BE7) the same three ($1838, $187E, $18C4); each height ($1C0C, $1C21) two, ahead ($190A) and up, which is the height itself ($1934). A value marked by the bit in zpa_BA is a place on the map, and the eye's place ($812D-$8132) is taken from it first. zpa_19 to zpa_1E give each list's last entry and count.
The VIC's memory settings for the two buffers: $F0 and $F8 for the window (screen at $7C00, bitmap at $4000 or $6000), $B0 and $B8 for the panel (screen at $EC00, bitmap at $C000 or $E000).

Starts the engine ($8115): swaps zero page for the engine's (swap_zp), banks the ROMs out ($01 = 5), clears the view and target states. On a C64, where $D030 reads $FF, it moves the second raster interrupt to $94B8 at line $9A. On a C128, where bit 0 of $D030 reads 0, it leaves it at $948F at line $32, which sets the C128's 1 MHz mode; the first interrupt sets 2 MHz, so a C128 runs the engine at twice the speed from line 251 to line 50, outside the picture. Then the raster interrupt is started (irq_on), the VIC set for the cockpit, and the map drawn (draw_map).
Stops the engine ($8118): the VIC back to bank 0, the text screen at $0400 and the KERNAL's characters, then s_918E.
Turns the sprites and the raster interrupt off (irq_off) and swaps zero page back (swap_zp).

Swaps $01-$FF with $3F01-$3FFF: the engine's zero page in for the flight, BASIC's and the KERNAL's back after it. G2 sets the flight's variables at $3F00 before it starts, and the debriefing reads them there after.
Points the RAM vectors at the engine's handlers, the IRQ at $9206 and the NMI and reset at $91EF, and starts the raster interrupt at line $FB.
Points the KERNAL's NMI vector at an RTI ($FEC1), sets the C128 back to 1 MHz, and stops the VIC's interrupt.
RESTORE: the key held with it is put in the keyboard buffer with bit 7 set (RUN/STOP becomes $FF, 4 becomes $B4).

The raster interrupt at line $FB, below the picture, once a frame. The window's background from zpa_C4; 2 MHz on a C128; the fire button read into zpa_CA, set only when it was let go since the last shot (zpa_C9); the next interrupt at line $9A; the window's buffer shown (from $910C); the sprites for the window set up from the values sprites_copy wrote into this routine; the sound effects (sound_step) and the keyboard (keyboard).

The line of the next interrupt: $32 as the file loads, for irq_c128 on a C128; engine_on patches it to $9A on a C64. The window's buffer is shown: the VIC's memory pointer from $910C by zpa_B1, and the same with bit 6 clear patched in at $94D3 for the panel, whose bitmap therefore changes with the window's; bank 1 ($DD00 = $96). The frame count zpa_17 goes up, and when new sprite values wait (zpa_2E) they are copied in (sprites_copy) and the bitmap mode set again.
The window's sprites' x high bits, patched in from $8174 (sprites_copy).
The window's eight sprites' x, the operands of these LDAs, five bytes apart, which sprites_copy writes from $8154-$815B.
The window's eight sprites' y, from $815C-$8163.
The window's eight sprites' colours, from $8164-$816B. Then the sound effects (sound_step) and the keyboard (keyboard).

With the CRT on the map, the heading strip's sprite (heading_sprite). The gun's flash ($81CD) and the missiles' sprites: an exploding one's frames, a flying one's flicker; every fourth frame the explosions' colours change at random.

The frame count's low three bits, patched in: once every eight frames, while missile slot 0 is not exploding, the shape of the sprite with that number is toggled between two frames (bit 0 of its pointer at $7FFA).

The enemy's gun flashes ($81D0), at random places; the missiles just fired from the wings (zpa_2F, zpa_30) as sprites; the screen's shake ($81CF) by the fine scroll, and the border's flash (zpa_CB). Then the next interrupt, at $94B8 on a C64.
The enemy gun flash's x, patched in at random every eight frames ($6C to $EB).

The enemy gun flash's y, patched in at random ($3A to $79). Sprite 2 shows the flash while $81D0 counts down, its shape stepping through $D2-$D5. Then the missiles just fired from the left and right wings (zpa_2F and zpa_30 count down), each a sprite (its number in zpa_31 or zpa_32) that moves outwards from the middle along the path at $E314 and $E328, its shapes from $E300 plus zpa_C7 or zpa_C8 for the weapon; the shake (the fine scroll at random while $81CF counts down) and the border's flash (a colour from $957A while zpa_CB counts down).
The low byte of the next interrupt's address, $B8, patched in by engine_on: $94B8 on a C64; on a C128 it stays $8F, for $948F.
The next interrupt's high byte, $94.
The C128's extra interrupt at line $32, the top of the picture: back to 1 MHz, and on to $94B8 at line $9A.

The raster interrupt at line $9A, where the window ends and the panel starts: the VIC to bank 3, the panel's bitmap and screen, black background, and the panel's eight sprites from the values sprites_copy wrote into this routine. Then back to $9206 at line $FB.
The panel sprites' X expansion, patched in: 2 (sprite 1 wide) while a missile is shown on the CRT, 0 when the CRT is on the map.
The panel's VIC memory pointer, patched in by the first interrupt: $B0 or $B8, the panel's bitmap at $C000 or $E000 with the window's buffer.
The panel sprites' Y expansion, patched in: 0.
The panel sprites' multicolour bits, patched in: 2 (sprite 1) while a missile is shown on the CRT.
The panel sprites' x high bits, patched in from $8195 (sprites_copy).
The panel's eight sprites' x, the operands of these LDAs, five bytes apart, which sprites_copy writes from $8175-$817C.
Panel sprite 1's x, patched in: $A0 while a missile is shown on the CRT.
The panel's eight sprites' y, from $817D-$8184.
Panel sprite 1's y, patched in: $B8 for the missile on the CRT.
The panel's eight sprites' colours, from $8185-$818C.
Panel sprite 1's colour, patched in: 7, yellow, for the missile on the CRT. Then the next interrupt is the one at $9206, line $FB.
The box's hit frames' counter: sprite 1 cycles $D9-$DC.
The colours the explosions flicker between, chosen at random every fourth frame.
A missile sprite's frame by distance, 16 steps, $77 far to $72 near, before the offset in zpa_B4.
The last frame put in $DFC0 for the CRT's copy of the homing missile.

Sets missile sprite x's frame from its distance (zpa_F5) through the table at $957E, plus zpa_B4 ($5F for an explosion's frames). In the target view, the locked target's homing missile is also copied to $DFC0 and shown on the CRT as a panel sprite.
The big map's drawing: the terrain map row's offset, counting down from $D0 to $20 in steps of $10 (s_9681).
The big map's drawing: the column, 2 to 13.
The hill test's pixel row on the map (from map_place); its low three bits pick the row within the character.
A work byte: twice the terrain square while the big map is drawn; the hill test's row times eight, then its pixel column.
zpa_18 less one, kept while the big map is drawn: its colours from $E300 are written only when this is 0.

Changes the view ($8112) to zpa_A5: 1 the big map, 2 and 3 the stores and damage pictures. From one of those, any change goes back to the cockpit. The map: the interrupt moved to $97D8, the colour RAM saved at $0400 (save_colours), bank 3 with the map's screen at $E800 and characters at $C800, and the map drawn.

Draws the big map: the middle 12 by 12 of the 16 by 16 squares from the terrain at $1A86 (columns 2-13, rows 13 down to 2 from the top), each three characters wide and two high, into screen columns 2-37 and rows 0-23 at $E800 (and the colour from $E300), then the units: each one seen (bit 4 of its type byte) as a character in its square, in the colour of its side and kind. With the big map not up only the screen is written.
Leaving the big map: back to the cockpit's colours (load_colours) and its interrupt (from $913B).
The raster interrupt while the big map is up: the sound effects, the keyboard, and the waypoint's cross blinking.
Each frame: on the big map, the helicopter's mark (sprite 1, block $40) at the helicopter's place; with a picture up, the picture's own code at $6C00.
A zero between two routines, never run or read.
Writes one row of a map square: three characters, their codes from x, and their colours from $E300 when the big map is up.
The rotor mark's step on the CRT's helicopter, which turns it each frame.

Builds sprite block $40 at $D000, in the RAM under the I/O: the helicopter's outline from $DF40 for its heading, and over it one of the rotor's four frames from $DF80, stepping with the rotor's speed.
The outline's place in $DF40, patched in from the heading: eight bytes written down the first column of the sprite's top eight rows.
The rotor mark's frame, patched in: one of four at $DF80-$DF9F, stepped on as the rotor's speed (zpa_41) adds up at $9872; it is ORed over the strip.
Clears the 64 bytes of sprite block $40 at $D000.

The map's hill test, $81CA: the position at $8148-$814B is turned into a map character and a pixel in it (map_place). A5 and A6 are $FF and 0 when that pixel is a hill's colour, 0 and 0 otherwise; A9 holds the character, $26 for a friendly base.
The hill test's pixel masks, by pixel place.
The hill test's masks for the hill colour, by pixel place.
Copies colour RAM to $0400-$07FF.
Copies $0400-$07FF back to colour RAM.
The picture's file name, one letter, set from the table after it.
The pictures' names: "1", the stores, and "2", the damage.

Shows picture file "1" (the stores) or "2" (the damage) from side 2: colour RAM saved, the VIC on the text screen at $6800 with characters at $6000, the sound off, the engine stopped and the KERNAL's zero page back (s_918E); then the KERNAL's SETLFS, SETNAM and LOAD. When the load worked and the file put $D8 at $6C00, its own code there is run; otherwise straight back to the cockpit.

The load's status (less bit 6, the end of the file) ORed with the first byte at $6C00, patched in: the picture's own code runs only when this is $D8, a CLD, and the status's bit 4, an error, is clear. Then the picture stays until picture_end.
Back from a picture: the window's first bitmap copied over the second ($4000 to $6000, 16 pages), the colours put back, the cockpit started again from $913B.
The sound effect's frame count.
The slide's SID register.
The slide's step, added each frame; 0 for none.
The slide's value now.

The sound effect player, once a frame: the effect's list is read for entries due at this frame's count; each writes a value to a SID register, or starts a slide that adds a step to one register each frame.
Starts effect zpa_A7 from the list of effects at zpa_A5-zpa_A6.
The window's bitmap pages, $40 and $60, by buffer.
The places in the interrupt routine of the panel sprites' register writes.
$810F: in the cockpit, shows the bitmap just drawn and makes the other the one to draw in (zpa_B1, zpa_BF), and asks the interrupt to take the new sprite values (zpa_2E).
Writes the 16 sprites' values from $8154-$8195 into the interrupt routines' LDA instructions, and the panel's pointers to $EFF8. On the cockpit it also handles the CRT's colour after a scale change.
Paints the radar scope's middle in the panel's screen (rows 21-23, columns 34-38) with the colour in $8220, and its centre cell with $B1, once after the scope's scale changes.
Clears the window in the hidden bitmap, 12 character rows of 256 bytes from the fifth column.
Paints the CRT's area (10 by 6 cells) in the panel's screen and colour RAM.
The CRT frame's screen colour, patched in by crt_next: $57 for the map.
The CRT frame's colour RAM colour, patched in: $0D for the map.

Unused: an entry ($8227 jumps here, and nothing calls $8227) that sets $9C1E to 1 and joins lamp_set after its table lookup, with its own place in zpa_A7 and shape in A, to write colour RAM even while the big map is up.
Lights lamp zpa_A5 in colour zpa_A6: a block of colour RAM from the table at $9C56, its low byte and its shape (the page, the width and the height); while the big map is up, into the copy at $0400.
1 to write the lamp into colour RAM whatever the view, patched in; lamp_set makes it 0, and then while the big map is up the lamp goes into the copy at $0400.
The lamps: for each, its colour RAM place (low byte) and its shape (page, width, height); lamp 0 here.
Each lamp's second byte, read with $9C56's: the page of colour RAM in bits 0-1, the width less one in bits 2-4 (7 means ten) and the height less one in bits 5-7.

The CRT, each frame. On the target view the locked target is drawn (target_view); with none the CRT goes on to the map. On the map, "TARGET" heads it while a target is locked, and the map's cross is drawn (crt_map). A message stays as it is.

$810C, SPACE: the CRT goes from the target view to the map; from the map to a waiting message, else to the target view when a target is asked for (zpa_FA not negative), else it stays on the map; from a message to the target view or the map, the same way. Each change sets the CRT's colours ($9BCB, $9BE4), painted a frame later (crt_frame).
How many frames the CRT's colour change waits.
Multiplies the signed number in A9-AA by the cosine of zpa_A8 ($9D3D), by its sine ($9D44), or by A ($9D49), an unsigned fraction of 256: the result in A6-A7, with the sign of AA and zpa_A8.
The low byte's product, patched in and added to the high byte's, with its carry; the result takes the sign of the two numbers'.
Multiplies zpa_A5 by Y, with x as the high byte of the sum to start: the result in A6-A7.
Divides A9-AA by zpa_A5 (with zpa_FD as its high byte), by shifting both and taking the reciprocal from $C500; a result too large is clamped to ±$3F.
Turns the position at $8148-$814B into the map's column (x) and row (Y), three characters to a square, for the cross and the hill test.
The low bytes of the big map screen's rows at $E800, 25 rows.
The high bytes of the big map screen's rows.

Draws the CRT's map: the part of the map around the helicopter, 6 rows of the map's characters copied from the screen at $E800 into the panel bitmap, only when the helicopter has moved to another square.
Where the CRT's map goes in each panel bitmap, low bytes: $30 and $30.
The same, high bytes: $F3 and $D3 (the CRT at $F330 in one buffer and $D330 in the other).
For each of the four pixel shifts, the bits of a map byte that go into the cell on the left: 00 03 0F 3F.
For each shift, the bits that go into the cell on the right: FF FC F0 C0.
Copies one row of map characters into the panel bitmap.
The map character's place in the map's character set, low byte, patched in: its code times eight.
Its high byte, $C8 plus the code's top bits. Each of the character's rows is shifted right by the cross's pixels ($A126) and merged into this byte of the CRT's bitmap and the next.
The bits of the right-hand byte that take the character, patched in: from $A047 by the pixel shift, and 0 at the CRT's last column.
The bits of the left-hand byte that take the character, patched in: 3 or more from $A043 after the first column, 0 for it.
The CRT's six character rows, offsets from its top-left cell, low bytes ($140 a row).
The CRT's six character rows' offsets, high bytes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6.
The bits shifted out of a map byte that go into the cell on the left.
The map row's pixel offset within its character (0-7), where the CRT window starts.
The CRT's character row being drawn, 0 to 5.
The map byte being copied along the row.
The first pixel row written in the CRT's character: 0, or 8 less $A120 for a map row's second half.
The map character's pixel row the copy stops before: 8, or $A120.
The map character's pixel row the copy starts at: $A120, or 0.
The pixel shift, the window's left column's low two bits.
The CRT's place in the panel bitmap being drawn, low byte (from $A03F).
The same, high byte (from $A041).
The map column at the CRT window's left edge: the helicopter's less 20, held inside the map.
The map row at the window's top edge: the helicopter's less 24, held inside the map.
For each hill, the outcode bits the line clipper tests (a_A163).
For a line partly hidden: draws only the part outside the hill's extent.
The line's outcode bits for off the right and off the left, patched in and tested against the entry for this hill at $A12B; a line that passes them widens the x range of the hills (zpa_08, zpa_09).

Draws the line zpa_19-zpa_20 in the window, clipped: each end gets its outcode (outcode); a line wholly outside on one side is dropped; one partly outside is cut by halving it until each end lies on an edge (clip_end). Keeps the hills' extents and draws through line.

The far end's y high byte, kept here while clip_end moves the near end onto the window's edge; when it is not negative the line is drawn. In the ground pass each line drawn widens the hill's extent (extent). A line with both ends outside is halved until its middle lies inside, up to ten times, and each half is then clipped (clip_end); a line wholly outside on one side goes to line_hidden instead.
Keeps zpa_08 and zpa_09 as the highest and lowest x drawn.
Widens the x range zpa_08 (highest) and zpa_09 (lowest) by A.
The outcode of one end (x = 0 or 4): bit 0 off the right, bit 3 off the left, bit 1 below, bit 2 above. The window is 128 by 96 pixels.
The window's width, $7F, or $27 for the CRT's target view, patched in, for the outcode's right edge.
The window's height, $5F, or $2F for the target view, patched in, for the outcode's bottom edge.
Swaps the line's two ends and their outcodes.
The clipper's window limits: x low, x high and y, patched for the CRT's target view.
The same limits' second set.
Moves one end of the line onto the window's edge by halving.
The height, patched in, to turn the near end's y over when the line crosses the bottom, so that one bisection serves every edge.
The height again, patched in, to turn the far end's y over.
The width, patched in, to turn the near end's x over when the line crosses the right edge.
The width again, patched in, to turn the far end's x over. Then the line is halved, the half that crosses the edge kept each time.
Where the bisection goes on, low byte, patched in from $A363 by the signs of the ends' y and x: $A408, $A43D or $A45F.
Its high byte, from $A366. The halving stops when the middle is within three pixels of the edge, which becomes the line's new end.
The window's height, patched in, to turn the new end's y back.
The window's width, patched in, to turn the new end's x back.
The address in the hidden bitmap of pixel (zpa_19, zpa_1B), from the row tables at $C3F0 and $C4B8: in zpa_FB, with the byte in Y and the pixel's place in x.
The window's place in its bitmap, low byte, patched in: $60, for $4160 or $6160, or $38 for the CRT's target view at $D338 or $F338.
The bitmap's page, patched in: $41 or $61 for the window in the buffer being drawn, $D3 or $F3 for the CRT.
Plots one pixel in the colour set by set_colour.
The colour's masks for one pixel, low byte, patched in by set_colour.
Draws a line from (zpa_19, zpa_1B) to (zpa_1D, zpa_1F) in the hidden bitmap, a pixel at a time, with separate loops for steep and shallow lines up and down.
The colour's masks for a shallow line going down, low byte, patched in by set_colour.
ORA (zp),Y, or AND (zp),Y to rub out, patched in (s_86D6): a shallow line going down is drawn a pixel at a time across, stepping down a row when its error overflows.
The shallow line's height, the error's step, patched in.
The shallow line's width, taken off the error when it overflows, patched in.
The colour's masks for a shallow line going up, patched in.
ORA or AND for a shallow line going up, patched in.
The rising shallow line's height, patched in.
The rising shallow line's width, patched in.
The colour's masks for a level line, patched in.
ORA or AND for a level line, patched in: a pixel after another along the row.
The colour's masks for a steep line going down, patched in.
ORA or AND for a steep line going down, patched in (set_plot_op): a pixel a row, stepping across when the error overflows.
The steep line's width, the error's step, patched in.
The steep line's height, patched in.
The colour's masks for a steep line going up, patched in.
ORA or AND for a steep line going up, patched in.
The rising steep line's width, patched in.
The rising steep line's height, patched in.
The first pixel's place in its byte, patched in. A steep line 32 rows long or more steps across by a fraction of 256, its width over its height, divided out first.
The colour's masks for a long steep line going down, patched in.
ORA or AND for a long steep line going down, patched in.
The long steep line's slope, a fraction of 256, patched in.
The colour's masks for a long steep line going up, patched in.
ORA or AND for a long steep line going up, patched in.
The rising long steep line's slope, patched in.
The first pixel's place in its byte, patched in. A shallow line 32 pixels across or more steps down by its height over its width, divided out first.
The colour's masks for a long shallow line going down, patched in.
ORA or AND for a long shallow line going down, patched in.
The long shallow line's slope, patched in.
The colour's masks for a long shallow line going up, patched in.
ORA or AND for a long shallow line going up, patched in.
The rising long shallow line's slope, patched in.

Sets the drawing colour in A: the line routines' mask operands are pointed at its four pixel masks, $81D1 plus four times the colour. Colours 0 to 3 draw; 4 and 5 are masks for rubbing out. Nothing is done when it is the colour set already ($A803).
The colour set last, patched in: asking for it again does nothing.
Fills the window from the top down: in each of the 32 columns, every byte is made sky ($FF) until a byte with a drawn pixel is found, which is filled to that pixel.
The keyboard scan, from the interrupt: with a key down, finds which (the first in the matrix) and, if it is not the one held last time, puts its code from the table at $A926 in the keyboard buffer.
The key codes in the keyboard matrix's order, 64: mostly PETSCII; the cursor keys $11 and $1D, the function keys $85-$88, left SHIFT $7D, right SHIFT $7C, C= $7E, RUN/STOP $7F.
The target found while drawing: its shape's address, low byte.
Its shape's address, high byte.
Its sideways offset in eye space, low byte.
Its sideways offset, high byte.
Its up-down offset, low byte.
Its up-down offset, high byte.
Its distance, low byte.
Its distance, high byte.
Its screen x.
Its screen y.
The next target's square, kept for right SHIFT.
The next target's slot; $FF none.
The target's size class.
The target view's scale by distance, 16 steps.
Returns.

Called for each object drawn. While a target is wanted (zpa_FA), an object of a kind that can be one, wholly in the window and nearer than $8147, is noted: the one after the target locked now, so that right SHIFT steps through them. Its place and size are kept for the target view ($A966-$A972).
Once a frame: the object noted becomes the locked target ($821D, $821E); with none, there is no target (zpa_FA = $FF).

Draws the locked target on the CRT: its box's place over the window (sprite 1), its distance printed, and its shape drawn large into the CRT's part of the panel bitmap, the line routines' limits and base address changed for it and put back after; its name follows (s_78C3).
Clears the CRT's area in the panel bitmap being drawn ($AC52), in the one at $C000 ($AC58) or at $E000 ($AC70), to the value in A.
Clears the CRT's area in the panel bitmap at $C000 (from $D338, under the I/O) to A.
Clears the CRT's area in the panel bitmap at $E000 (from $F338) to A.
Eight filler bytes, $EE $DE four times, between two routines; nothing runs or reads them.
The missiles' own jump table: $AC90 a missile's sprite, $AC93 clear it, $AC96 launch, $AC99 move all, $AC9C the locked target's unit, $AC9F and $ACA2 the radar list, $ACA5 the scope.
$AC93: hide the missile's sprite (j_ADE9).

Launches a missile, if a slot is free (free_slot): from the position at $8148-$814D, on heading zpa_A5, of kind zpa_A6, at target zpa_A7. Its speed, turn, life and guidance come from the tables at $ADF2-$AE19; a Hellfire takes the locked target. A missile at the player picks the sprite for the warning on the panel.

The missile's turn rate, patched in, so that its lower limit ($B5BA) is the rate's negative. Then its life ($8217), hit distance ($B5DE), target ($B5C6), heading ($B5B4) and speed ($B5CC); an unguided one (bit 3) takes its steps from zpa_A8-zpa_AA. A Sidewinder or an FFAR (bits 3 and 4) is aimed at the locked target (s_B503). A player's missile fired while looking ahead is shown leaving a wing: from the wing that is not damaged (damage bits 10 and 11), FFARs from both at once, the others from each in turn by the stores' count.

The operand of the BNE above, which the table after it is read from as its entry 0: the wing sprites' shapes by weapon (1 Sidewinder, 2 FFAR, 3 Hellfire), for the left at $AD54-$AD56 and the right at $AD57-$AD59.
The left wing's launch sprites by weapon: $DD for a Sidewinder, $78 for an FFAR, $DD for a Hellfire (blocks $DD-$E0 and $78-$7B, four frames each).
The Hellfire's left wing shape, $DD; the table's entry 3.
The right wing's: $C4, $7C and $C4 (blocks $C4-$C7 and $7C-$7F).
Both wings whole: an FFAR pair leaves from both wings at once, its left sprite in slot 1 or 2; any other missile from the left wing or the right by whether its store's count ($53D8) is odd or even.
Sets panel sprite Y's pointer and its count.
Puts the missile's sprite at its place in the window, or hides it.
The eight missile kinds' speed classes: 0 the Sidewinder, 1 the FFAR, 2 the Hellfire, 3-7 the enemy's.
The kinds' turn rates: $B5C0 gets it, $B5BA its negative.
The kinds' lives: how many passes each flies ($8217).
The kinds' hit distances ($B5DE).
The kinds' guidance: bit 7 the locked target, bit 6 radar, bit 5 infrared, bit 4 the Hind, bit 3 none; bits 1 and 2 ignore the jammers. Sidewinder $10, FFAR $08, Hellfire $80.
A homing missile's view: a target more than $20 off its heading either way is lost.
The other edge, $E0.

Moves the six missiles, once a pass. A homing one steers towards its target: a radar one is lost to the radar jammer (unless its kind ignores it) and decoyed by chaff while it falls, an infrared one likewise by the infrared jammer and flares; a Sidewinder goes for the Hind; a Hellfire for the locked target.
Turns the missile towards the target by at most its turn rate, from the table of sixteen headings at $B512.
Its step along the heading from the sine tables at $B522 and $B563, scaled by its speed.
Its climb or dive towards the target's height, at most the step.
Moves it; near the target it moves in steps of 127 to test each for a hit.
A hit: on the helicopter ($81B3), or on chaff or a flare ($81B2), or on a unit, which explodes; the missile is gone when its life runs out or it hits the ground.

An exploding missile's timer; at the end the unit it hit is destroyed ($81B4) when the missile's guidance flags ($8211, less bit 0) match those $AE12 holds for the missile kind $B5A4 names for the unit's kind; unit 5, the Hind, falls to any missile ($B309).
The missile's distance class, for its sprite's size.
The homing flags into $81AE, and on to the next missile.
The locked target's unit number in zpa_A5: the Hind (5), a unit found by its identity in $5200 and $5280, or $7F for none.
Whether the missile is within its hit distance ($B5DE) of the target, in x plus y and in height: A = 1 if so.

The differences from missile x to target Y: the helicopter, chaff, flares and the Hind (0-5) have fine positions, the units only the high bytes of theirs. Their sizes and which of sixteen directions the target lies in (zpa_08: the signs of x and y, which difference is larger, and whether it is at least twice the other) for steering.
Halves the step and adds it ($B4B8), or adds it ($B4C0), to the move.
Adds the step zpa_21-zpa_24 to the move zpa_1D-zpa_20.
LDA #0 and RTS, a routine nothing in the flight calls.
Finds a free missile slot, takes it in $81AC and returns it in x and A; negative if all six are in use.
Frees missile slot x.
Sets missile x's target to the locked one.
The distance classes' limits for a missile sprite's size: 1, 2, 4 and 8.
The heading of each of the sixteen directions target_delta tells apart (zpa_08), $10 apart, for turning towards a target.
A missile's sideways step for each 64th of a quarter turn between its heading and the view's: a sine, 0 to $FF over 65 entries.
Its forward step: the cosine, $FF to 0.

For each unit kind, the missile kind that can destroy it: 1 the FFAR, 2 the Hellfire, 0 the Sidewinder. Any other kind that hits does nothing. No unit in the five theatres has kind 14 or 15, and the Hind, unit 5, skips this table ($B309).
The six missiles' headings.
The six missiles' negative turn limits.
The six missiles' turn limits.
The six missiles' targets: a unit number.
The six missiles' speed classes.
The six missiles' climb steps, low bytes.
The six missiles' climb steps, high bytes.
The six missiles' hit distances.
The six missiles' distance classes, for their sprites' sizes.
Puts the helicopter's position into one of the fine-position slots (0 the helicopter, 1 the chaff, 2 the flares), so missiles can home on it.
Adds unit zpa_A5 to the radar scope's list of ten; zpa_A5 = 1 if there was room.
Takes unit zpa_A5 off the list; zpa_A5 = 0 if it was on it.

Draws the radar scope, $81AF: the dots of the last frame in this buffer are rubbed out from the lists at $B886-$B8F1, then the units on the list, the missiles and the Hind are plotted, turned by the heading and scaled by $81CE. A change of scale repaints the scope's colours once.
The address of a dot to rub out, low byte, patched in from $B8AA.

Its high byte, from $B886; the byte it changed is put back from $B8CE. Then, at a change of scale ($81CE), the scope's colour is set from $B84E. The helicopter's own place is the scope's middle; the units on the radar's list at $B8F2 are drawn as dots in colour $FF, the six missiles in $AA, and the Hind in $AA or $FF by buffer, so that it flickers between two colours.
The scope's dot colours by buffer: $AA and $FF.
Scales a position for the scope.
Plots one dot on the scope, if it falls inside its circle ($B850, $B86B), remembering the byte it changed.
The pixel's mask in its byte, patched in from $81E9: the dot is drawn in colour zpa_21, and its address and the byte it changed are kept ($B886, $B8AA, $B8CE) to rub it out next time.
Turns the scope's dot by the heading.
The scope's dots counted, one for each buffer.
The radar scope's colours by its scale ($81CE): $B1 and $01.
The scope's circle: for each row, its left edge.
The scope's circle: for each row, its right edge.
The scope's remembered dots: their bitmap addresses, low bytes, for both buffers.
The remembered dots' addresses, high bytes.
The bytes the dots changed, to be put back.
The units on the radar scope, a list of ten.
How many dots were drawn last time.
The instruments' jump table.
$B906: draw the seven bar gauges (gauges).
$B915: print a number on the CRT (print_crt_number).

Draws the dials: the heading printed in figures and the height in hundreds, then four needles (airspeed, altimeter, vertical speed and the heading compass), each redrawn only when its value has changed, by a short line in its sprite.
One needle's line, from the tables at $BB5E-$BBCA.
The needles' sprite blocks, low bytes: $00, $40, $80, $C0.
Each needle's sprite x, before the step for its quarter.
Each needle's sprite y, before the step for its quarter.
The sprite's x step by the quarter of the turn the needle points into: 0, 0, -22, -22, so the sprite's corner stays at the dial's centre.
The sprite's y step by quarter: -20, 0, 0, -20.
The needle's 22 lines, one for each slope: the length in steps, also the divisor of the slope's fraction.
The lines' starting fraction for a steep line.
The lines' starting fraction for a shallow line.
The lines' across step for a steep line, out of the length: 0 for straight up.
The lines' up step for a shallow line; equal to the length when the line is steep.
The line (0-21) for each of the 65 angles from 0 to a quarter turn, the last read for a needle pointing at a quarter's start from the far side.
The four multicolour pixels in a byte, right to left: 03 0C 30 C0.
Each line's far end for a needle in the third quarter: the pixel in the top two bits, the byte in the sprite in the low six.
The same for the fourth quarter.
Each needle's first sprite block, $80-$83.
Each needle's second sprite block, $84-$87.
Each needle's bit in the sprites' x high bits (sprites 4-7).
The same bits inverted, to clear them. The eight bytes after these four are never read.
Each needle's buffer page now, $E0 or $E1.
Each needle's last value, so it is redrawn only on a change.
The heading compass's rose.
For the compass needle pointing into the southern half, where its shape starts in $BCAE, by eighth of a turn.
The compass needle's eight shapes, four bytes (four rows of one sprite byte) each, one for each eighth of a turn.

Draws the attitude indicator from the pitch and roll ($813A, $813B), only when they have changed: the horizon bar's two ends move a step at a time towards the new ones, each step rubbed out and drawn again in both panel bitmaps.
The point on the indicator's circle for an angle.
How far the horizon line turns round the dial for the roll (a quarter of $813B, 0-5).
Half the angle between the horizon line's two ends, by half the pitch (0-10): $40, a line through the centre, when level, less as the nose goes up or down.
The dial's quarter circle: each point's x from the centre, in pixels.
Each point's y from the centre, in rows.
The point (0-24) on the quarter circle for each of the 64 angles in a quarter turn.
Draws a line in both panel bitmaps, in the colour in A.
INX ($E8) for a line going right, DEX ($CA) going left, patched in: the step to the next pixel.
The pixel place past the byte's last, patched in: 4 going right, $FF going left.
The pixel place the next byte starts at, patched in: 0 going right, 3 going left.
The step to the next byte, patched in: 8 going right, -8 going left. The line is drawn a pixel at a time across, stepping down a row when its error overflows, in both panel bitmaps.
The horizon line's two ends now, as angles round the dial ($C01C and $C01D), each moving two steps a pass towards $C01E-$C01F.
The horizon line's second end now.
The angles the two ends are moving to (with $C01F).
The second end's target.
Each end moved two steps towards the top of the dial (with $C021): the line drawn in colour 3 just above the horizon.
The second end's point above the horizon.
Half the pitch, worked on while the ends are found.
A work byte: the pitch's sign, then each end's angle rounded to an even step.
A work byte: a quarter of the roll, the line's turn round the dial, then how many ends moved this pass.
The colour of the line being drawn: $FF or 0.
The line drawer's count of rows left in the current character.
The pitch the dial last showed.
The roll the dial last showed.
Draws the seven bar gauges from $813D-$8143, each moving one step a frame towards its value (all the way at once when bit 7 is set), in both panel bitmaps.

The label is a false one: the BIT at $381C hides an LDA #$C0 and names this address by chance. Here the bar's new top moves to the next character row; the row under it is painted colour 3, both panel bitmaps. A value with bit 7 set goes round again until the bar reaches it.
The seven bars' bottom rows.
The seven bars' columns.
The bar pixel masks.
The seven bars' heights now, moving a step a frame.

Prints the number in $813C on the CRT, for the target view: into the bitmap being drawn only, on the CRT's background pattern ($55), in one figure when A is 0 and two otherwise. The operands it patches are put back after.
Prints the number in $813C at column X, row Y in two figures, keeping a leading zero.
Prints the number in $813C in one figure.
Prints the number in $813C in two figures, a leading zero left blank.

Prints the heading in $813C (0 to 255 for a full turn) as a bearing of three figures, 0 to 359 degrees: the quarter from the tables at $C3E7 and $C3EB (0, 90, 180, 270) and the degrees within it from $C3A7.
Prints the number in $813C in three figures, leading zeros left blank.

Prints the number in $813C as up to three decimal figures (as many as $C250 says, set by the callers) into both panel bitmaps at column zpa_FD (in pixels of two) and row zpa_FE; X = 0 leaves leading zeros blank. Each figure is five rows of the font at $C344, shifted to its pixel place.

How many figures to print, less one, patched in by the callers ($C130, $C142, $C152): 2 for three. A zero before the first figure that is not is left blank ($0A, the font's blank) unless leading zeros are kept.
The figure's place in the font at $C344, low byte, patched in: eight bytes to a figure.
Its high byte. The figure's five rows are shifted right by the pixel place (zpa_FD) into $C399 and $C39E, its left and right parts.
$20, patched to 0 for the target view: the second bitmap's address is the first's with this toggled, so the figures go into both panel bitmaps or, for the CRT, only into the one being drawn.
The same toggle for the right part's second address.
The mask for the figure's left byte, low byte, patched in: from $C30A, eight bytes for each pixel place.
The left mask's high byte.
ORed into the left byte, patched in: 0, or $55 for the CRT's target view.
The mask for the figure's right byte, low byte, patched in: $1D on from the left's.
The right mask's high byte.
ORed into the right byte, 0 or $55 for the CRT. Then on to the next figure, eight bytes to the right.
Powers of ten, 1, 10 and 100, that the printer takes away to find each figure.
Three bytes, 5, 5 and 2, that nothing reads.
The bits a figure leaves alone in its left byte, five rows for each of four pixel shifts eight bytes apart: $03, $C0, $F0, $FC. The printer patches the operand at $C2C5 to the shift's rows.
Shift 1's rows of the left masks, $C0, where the patched operand pointed when the snapshot was taken.
The bits a figure leaves alone in its right byte, by shift: $FF, $FF, $3F, $0F (the operand at $C2DC).
Shift 1's rows of the right masks.
The panel's figures: 0 to 9 and a blank (10), each five rows of three pixels, eight bytes apart. The printer patches its LDA at $C287 to the figure's rows.
Figure 9's rows, where the patched LDA last read.
The figure being printed, shifted into place: its left byte's five rows.
Its right byte's five rows.
Non-zero once a figure other than 0 has been printed, or set to 1 by a caller before any (print_bearing, so that a bearing keeps its leading zeros); while it is 0 a zero is left blank.
The number's three figures, hundreds first ($C3A4-$C3A6).
The tens figure.
The units figure.
The degrees for each 64th of a quarter turn: 0 to 89.
The degrees at the start of each quarter turn, low bytes: 0, 90, 180, 14 (270).
The same, high bytes: 0, 0, 0, 1. Its fifth byte is not read.
The bitmap's 200 pixel rows: each row's address, low byte.
Each pixel row's address, high byte, less the bitmap's base: 200 entries to $C57F.
Pixel rows 72 to 199's high bytes; the divider also reads its reciprocals from here, with X from 128 to 255, so they lie at $C580.
Pixel rows 136 to 199's high bytes.
The reciprocals: 32768 divided by each number from 128 to 255, less one: $FF down to $7F.
The sine table: the size of the sine for each of 256 angles, 0 to $FF; a half turn takes 128 entries and the second half repeats the first, the sign being the callers'.
The arctangent: for each n from 0 to 255, the angle whose tangent is n/64, in 256ths of a turn ($00 to $36).
The map's character set, the theatre's own (Western Europe's here), copied from $A800 by the loader before the flight. Characters 0-31: letters and the shapes the CRT also prints figures with.
Character 7, G, where the CRT's message printer, which patches its address, last read a letter.
Map font characters 15-31: letters O to Z and the shapes after them.
Characters 32-57: the unit symbols of the map; $26 is a friendly base.
Characters 58-255: the terrain, six characters to a terrain, three wide and two high, 33 terrains. The CRT's map and the big map are made of them; the hill test reads their pixels.
Characters 128-255, the second half of the terrain.
Character 235, where the CRT's map copy, which patches its address, last read a row.
Map font characters 243-255, the last terrain characters.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 13: the canopy's frame at both ends, the tops of the airspeed dial (columns 6-14), the CRT (15-24) and the altimeter (25-33).

The panel bitmap at $C000, row 14: the left frame with a lamp (columns 4-5), the airspeed dial, the CRT's title line (15-24), where RADIO MSG, TARGET and the targets' names are printed, the altimeter and the right frame's lamp box.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 15, columns 0-14: the left canopy frame with the letters F and T over the fuel and torque bars, and the airspeed dial's 50 mark.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 15, columns 25-39: the altimeter's figures 8 to 2 round its top, and the canopy's right frame with its lamp box.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 16, columns 0-14: the fuel bars (yellow) and torque bars (blue), and the airspeed dial with its 200 mark.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 16, columns 25-39: the altimeter's 7 and 3, and the lamp box.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 17, columns 0-14: the fuel and torque bars, and the airspeed dial's 100 mark.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 17, columns 25-39: the altimeter's box for the hundreds (printed by the engine), and the lamp box.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 18, columns 0-14: the bars' feet and the airspeed dial's 150 mark.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 18, columns 25-39: the altimeter's 6, 5 and 4, and the lamp box's foot.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 19, columns 0-14: the heading compass's top, the letter R over the three bars of engine 1, the rotor and engine 2, and the top of the attitude indicator.

The panel bitmap at $C000, row 19, columns 8-13: the top of the attitude indicator. The lamp routine's ADC #$D8 makes colour RAM addresses that the disassembler names here; the RAM itself is only this picture.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 19, the last twelve bytes before the CRT: the attitude indicator's right edge. The LDX at $9D28 reads $D82C as colour RAM, the CRT's frame colour, from the chips.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 19, columns 25-39: the top of the vertical speed dial and of the radar scope's circle.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 20, columns 0-14: the heading compass, the R bars and the attitude indicator's sky.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 20, columns 25-39: the vertical speed dial's upper marks and the radar scope.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 20, columns 32-39: the radar scope's upper part. Named by the CRT's colour RAM writes ($9BE7), which reach the chips, not this RAM.
The panel bitmap at $C000, the last byte of row 20, at the right edge of the radar scope; $DA3F is a colour RAM address to the code that names it.

The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21: the bottoms of the R bars and the heading compass (columns 0-6), the attitude indicator (7-14), the stores' upper pictures: a Sidewinder, an FFAR and a Hellfire (15-24), the vertical speed dial (25-33) and the radar scope (34-39).
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21, from the last byte of column 4 to column 9: the compass's foot and the attitude indicator's left part; $DA67 is the CRT's colour RAM to the code ($9BE7).
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21, columns 9-14: the attitude indicator; $DA8F is the CRT's colour RAM to the code.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21, columns 14-19: the attitude indicator's right edge and the Sidewinder's picture; $DAB7 is colour RAM to the code.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21, columns 19-24: the FFAR's and the Hellfire's pictures; $DADF is colour RAM to the code.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21, the first seven bytes of column 24, in the Hellfire's picture; $DB00 is colour RAM to the lamps.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21, columns 24-29: the stores' right edge and the vertical speed dial's left part; $DB07 is colour RAM to the code.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21, columns 29-39: the vertical speed dial's right part and the radar scope; $DB2F is colour RAM to the code.
The panel bitmap at $C000, row 21, the last 17 bytes: the radar scope's right edge.

The panel bitmap at $C000, row 22: the heading in three figures (columns 0-2) and the bars' feet, the attitude indicator, the counts of Sidewinders, FFARs and Hellfires (15-24), the vertical speed dial and the radar scope.

The panel bitmap at $C000, row 22, columns 37-39: the radar scope's right edge. The STA at $B66A, which puts back the bytes the scope's dots changed, is patched with each dot's address and last pointed here.

The panel bitmap at $C000, row 23: the strip that the slip and waypoint marks slide along (columns 0-6), the attitude indicator, the stores' lower pictures: chaff, the cannon and a flare (15-24), the vertical speed dial and the radar scope.

The panel bitmap at $C000, row 24: a label and the waypoint's bearing in three figures (columns 0-6), the bottom of the attitude indicator, the counts of chaff, rounds and flares (15-24), the vertical speed dial's foot and the radar scope's.
The helicopter seen from above, for each eighth of a turn of its heading: eight frames of eight rows, one byte each, which make the CRT's helicopter mark (sprite block $40 at $D000).
The rotor seen from above, four frames of eight rows (a diagonal, upright, the other diagonal, across), laid over the outline as the rotor turns.
The rotor's fourth frame, across, where the patched LDA at $98B0 last read.
Sprite block $7F: the CRT's copy of the locked target's homing missile, written while the target view shows it.

The map's unit bits: for each of its 256 squares (16 by 16, the edge always 0), a bit for each switchable object still standing. Destroying a unit clears its bit; the view draws only the objects whose bits are set.

The wing launches' frames: for each of the 20 steps of a missile leaving the wing, the frame to add to the wing's sprite, 3 down to 0. These 60 bytes ($E300-$E33B) lie over the colours of map characters 0-59, which the big map and the hill test read here too.
The wing launches' x step from the wing, by step: 0 growing to $72.
The wing launches' y by step: $70 to $8D.
The map characters' colours by character code, here from 60 to 255, which the big map writes to colour RAM and the hill test reads.
The rotor's target speed by the engines that run (none, engine 1, engine 2, both), low bytes: 0, $C0, $C0, $80.
The same, high bytes: 0, 0, 0, 1 (both engines: $180).
The joystick's two bits for an axis to a step: both pressed 0, the second pressed +1, the first -1, neither 0.

Reads the joystick in port 2 into zpa_7A (up -1, down +1) and zpa_84 (left -1, right +1). Both are zeroed unless the high bytes of CIA 2's timers A and B are $7D to $80 apart: the library started them $7F00 apart on side 1, and they keep that while they run.

Reads unit A's record into zpa_53-zpa_59: its x and y ($5100, $5180, high bytes), its alert byte ($5280), its type byte ($5300) and $5380. Units 0-5 also have fine positions: the low bytes, the height and the heading.
Writes zpa_53-zpa_59 back as unit A's record.
The bearing of the vector (A7-A8, A5-A6), 0 to 255 for a full turn: the octant from the signs and which is larger, and the angle within it from the ratio (s_E601) through the table at $E55D.
The bearing's angles within an octant, 128 entries by the ratio of the smaller difference to the larger: $40 to $80.
Entries 64 to 127 of the angles.
Negates the word at A5+x.
Swaps A5-A6 with A7-A8.
Shifts A right Y times.
Divides A7-A8 by A5-A6, signed, into A5-A6.
Makes the word at A5+x positive, noting the sign.

The challenge at a friendly base, a step each time zpa_89 runs out. First the CRT shows PASSWORD: with the codeword's letters and asks for the countersign, typed with the letter keys, DEL and RETURN; a checksum of it must match the codeword's in the table at $E741. Right, the challenge is over. Wrong, "INCORRECT COUNTRSIGN SEND AGAIN" and a second try; wrong again, "FALSE COUNTRSIGN DESTROY INTRUDING HELICOPTER" and every damage bit set.
The 16 codewords' countersign checksums, one each; the challenge compares the typed countersign's checksum with the entry for the mission's codeword.
Takes the first key from the keyboard buffer: A = its code, 0 (and Z set) if none.
The big map screen's last 16 bytes, after its 1,000 cells, which the screen does not show.
The big map screen's sprite pointers: sprite 0's, $B7, the waypoint's cross, set by draw_map.
Sprite 1's pointer on the big map: $40, the helicopter's mark.
Sprites 2-7's pointers on the big map, unused there.

The sound effects' addresses in this page, low bytes, ten effects. Each effect is a list of three-byte entries: the frame it is due in, a SID register (0-24) and the value written there; a frame with bit 7 set starts a slide instead, its start value (whose low three bits pick the register) then the step added each frame. A 0 ends it.
Six bytes before the first effect that nothing reads.
Effect 0: a triangle tone on voice 1 with noise on voice 3, sliding up twice, two seconds. None of the flight's calls asks for it.
Effect 1, the cannon: a pulse on voice 1, gated for 30 frames.
Effect 2, chaff, a flare or stores jettisoned: a noise burst of 16 frames.
Effect 3, a missile's end: noise sliding down for 90 frames.
Effect 4, a jammer switched: a sawtooth swept up, its step patched to $40 for the radar jammer and $10 for the infrared one ($EC7C).
The jammer sound's sweep step, patched by the key that switches the jammer.
Effect 5, a missile hitting the helicopter: four frames of noise.
Effect 6, a missile fired: noise rising then falling for two seconds.
The launch sound's rising step, patched to 1 for a Sidewinder or Hellfire and 9 for an FFAR.
Inside the launch sound. The BIT at $373D names this address by chance: it hides an LDX #$EC.
Effect 7, a gun hit, a crash, an explosion or a decoyed missile: a short noise.
Effect 8, a one-frame triangle blip: an enemy missile fired, or the CRT moved on to a target.
The blip's pitch, patched: $14 for an enemy launch, $3C for the CRT.

Effect 9, an engine's starter: effect 0's slides the other way. Its first entry names register $50, past the SID's 25: the SID repeats its registers every 32 bytes, so the write lands in register 16, voice 3's pulse width low byte; effect 0's names register 1.
23 bytes after the last effect, like the end of effect 0, that nothing reads.
Sprite block $B4: the attitude indicator's pitch ladder, panel sprite 0.
Sprite block $B5: the slip mark, a small triangle pointing down, panel sprite 2 on the strip under the heading.
Sprite block $B6: the waypoint mark, a small triangle pointing up, panel sprite 3.
Sprite block $B7: a cross, the waypoint's on the big map (sprite 0 there).
Eight zero bytes between the sprites and the panel's colours, never read.
